title: Finite positive affine rank pieces for a finite locally free morphism with a section
statement: Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $f:X\to Y$ be finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and let $a:Y\to X$ satisfy $f\circ a=\mathrm{id}_Y$. For $y\in Y$ with residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field], write $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and $d(y)=\dim_{\kappa(y)}\Gamma(X_y,\mathcal O_{X_y})$. Then $d(y)\geq1$ for every $y$. The sets $Y_r=\{y:d(y)=r\}$, for integers $r\geq0$, are pairwise disjoint open-and-closed subsets with union $Y$ and $Y_0=\varnothing$. With their open-subscheme structures [def-weil-open-immersion], every $Y_r$ and $X_r=f^{-1}(Y_r)$ is affine, and $f_r:X_r\to Y_r$ is finite locally free of degree $r$. Moreover there are idempotents $b_r\in A$ and $b'_r\in B$, meaning $b_r^2=b_r$ and $(b'_r)^2=b'_r$, such that $Y_r=D(b_r)$ and $X_r=D(b'_r)$, where $D(b)=\{\mathfrak p:b\notin\mathfrak p\}$. The set $I=\{r\geq1:Y_r\ne\varnothing\}$ is finite, $Y=\coprod_{r\in I}Y_r$, and $Y=\varnothing$ implies $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 03BI (groupoids-lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free), positive-degree argument, and Tag 03BJ (groupoids-lemma-integral-over-invariants), first proof paragraph, abstracted to an affine finite locally free morphism admitting a section; rank strata: Morphisms Tag 04MH (morphisms-lemma-finite-locally-free); clopen affine pieces: Algebra Tags 00E8 (algebra-lemma-quasi-compact) and 00EE (algebra-lemma-disjoint-decomposition), Schemes Tag 01I3 (schemes-lemma-standard-open-affine).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant] to $f$. Its fibre dimension is exactly $d(y)$, so it is finite and locally constant, its level sets $Y_r$ are clopen, $Y=\coprod_{r\geq0}Y_r$, and $f^{-1}(Y_r)\to Y_r$ is finite locally free of degree $r$. Distinct level sets are disjoint because an integer cannot have two distinct values.

Fix y. The section identity gives f(a(y))=y, hence the fibre over y is nonempty, using Scheme.Hom.fiberHomeo from [def-pc-fibre-product]. The ring of global sections of a nonempty scheme is nontrivial (evaluation at a stalk, a nontrivial local ring, sends 0 and 1 to distinct elements). Step 1 supplies finite-dimensionality over the residue field with its canonical algebra structure. Module.finrank_pos therefore gives d(y)>=1. Thus Y_0 is empty. This uses the standard affine spectrum and residue-field conventions [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 03BI (groupoids-lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free), exclusion of rank zero; explicit section argument abstracted from the groupoid unit.

proof.text: For each $r$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] to the clopen subset $Y_r\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$, obtaining $b_r^2=b_r$ and $Y_r=D(b_r)$. A scheme morphism is continuous, so $X_r=f^{-1}(Y_r)$ is clopen in $\operatorname{Spec}B$; apply the same node with ring $B$ to obtain $(b'_r)^2=b'_r$ and $X_r=D(b'_r)$. This also applies to empty strata, where one can choose the zero idempotent.

Mathlib IsAffineOpen.Spec_basicOpen makes each principal open D(b_r) and D(b′_r) affine. Its proof encapsulates [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] and the identification with its image open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Rewrite by the two basic-open equalities from step 3. The finite locally free degree-r restrictions are already supplied by step 1.

source.place: Tag 01I3 (schemes-lemma-standard-open-affine), proof via localization open immersion.

proof.text: The affine target is compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply IsLocallyConstant.range_finite to its fibre-degree function. Every nonempty rank stratum witnesses a value in that finite range, so I={r | 1<=r and Y_r nonempty} is finite. Each point y lies in the piece indexed by d(y), and positivity puts this index in I. The indexed open inclusions are pairwise disjoint, since equality of subtype indices follows from equality of their natural-number values. Apply AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_isColimit_cofanMk_of to these covering disjoint open immersions to get the required cofan colimit. If Y is empty, membership in I would give a point of Y, a contradiction, so I is empty.
